meta.scope: Applying for NSHD data. Answers come from the OWL Data Sharing page and the Skylark Access page.

entries.question: How do I apply for NSHD data?
entries.keywords: apply application how to get data request start begin steps process requesting access request access apply for data
entries.answer:
Each application is for one project and a set of variables. The steps are:

  1. Choose the variables you need by searching or browsing OWL, Condor or the data dictionary.
  2. Complete the data dictionary.
  3. Upload it to Condor to finalise your basket.
  4. Submit the Data Access Request Form, attaching the completed data dictionary.
  5. NSHD reviews your application.
  6. If approved, your data is made available through the UCL Data Safe Haven.

I want to request access to the data

entries.question: What is the data dictionary and do I have to complete one?
entries.keywords: data dictionary spreadsheet excel mark y request variable column complete fill download template
entries.answer:
It is an Excel spreadsheet where you mark Y against every variable you want. Only variables marked in the "Request variable" column are included in your application.

You can complete it by hand, or build your basket on OWL and download a copy that is already marked for you.

entries.answer: Search or browse OWL, Condor or the data dictionary. On OWL you can search the data dictionary, browse by category, view popular variables, search by year or longitudinally, use the UK LLC catalogue, and see what other projects asked for.

entries.question: What happens after I submit?
entries.keywords: after submit submitted happens next process review committee approved approval stages reviews reviewed reviewer who decides decision assess assessed confidentiality sign agreement stages
entries.answer:
1. Your request is logged and the data sharing team is notified.
  2. The data sharing committee reviews it and either approves it or asks you questions.
  3. You complete the confidentiality forms, which are emailed to you as each stage finishes.
  4. Once everything is approved, your basket is built and the data is made available through the UCL Data Safe Haven.

entries.question: What is a basket ID?
entries.keywords: basket id identifier number condor attach quote reference application form id
entries.answer: When you finalise your basket in Condor it is given an ID. Add it to the Data Access Request Form, or send it later with the Additional Users / Data Request form. Quote the application form ID you were given, so the basket is matched to the right project.

entries.question: My basket has more than 500 variables. Is that a problem?
entries.keywords: 500 over large limit split too many maximum big basket variables
entries.answer: Condor splits a large basket automatically into saved baskets of no more than 500 variables. They are reviewed together as one overall request, so you may be asked to justify it, and it may take longer to process.

entries.answer: Restricted variables can be added to your data dictionary on OWL, but they are not imported automatically when you upload it to Condor. Each one has to be requested separately. Hover over the padlock next to a variable on OWL to see who to contact about it.

entries.question: What is the difference between OWL, Condor and Skylark?
entries.keywords: difference owl condor skylark what is which platform systems tools
entries.answer:
• OWL is where you discover variables. It is public and needs no registration.
  • Condor holds the full set of variables. It is where you finalise, save and share your basket, and it needs a registered account.
  • Skylark is the data access information and forms portal.

entries.question: How do I get a Condor account?
entries.keywords: condor account register registration sign up login log in username approve approved access
entries.answer:
1. Use Register in the Condor menu and complete every field marked with an asterisk.
  2. Email your username to MRCLHA.Swiftinfo@ucl.ac.uk so your account can be approved.
  3. LHA contacts you by email to confirm. Add their address to your safe senders list.
